# Morphometic analysis
```{r, label="import spores",results="hide", echo=F, cache=T, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
# Import outlines: First list jpeg files to import

jpg.list <- list.files("outlines", pattern=c( ".jpg"), full.names=TRUE) 

# import them

spores <- Momocs::import_jpg(jpg.paths = jpg.list, auto.notcentered = T)
out_spores <- Momocs::Out(spores)
out_spores <- Momocs::coo_center(out_spores)
out_spores_scaled <- Momocs::coo_scale(out_spores)
out_spores_smoothed <- Momocs::coo_smooth(out_spores_scaled, n = 5)
# Ensure all outlines have the same number of points (e.g., 100 points per outline)
out_spores_interp <- Momocs::coo_interpolate(out_spores_smoothed, n = 120)
# Now apply Procrustes alignment
out_spores_aligned <- Momocs::fgProcrustes(out_spores_interp)
# Visualize to confirm
panel(out_spores_aligned, title = "Aligned Amanita Spores after Resampling")
efourier_spores <- Momocs::efourier(out_spores_scaled, nb.h = 10, norm = TRUE)
pca_spores <- Momocs::PCA(efourier_spores)

```

# Volume (size) analysis

```{r}
# Load the spore volume data
volume_data <- read_csv("spreadsheets/Sporelengthwidthvolume.csv")

# View the first few rows to confirm it's loaded correctly
head(volume_data)

```

# clean pca data and prep for data merge
```{r}
# Extract PCA scores and add species names if available
pca_scores_df_species <- as.data.frame(pca_spores$x)  # PCA scores
pca_scores_df_species$species <- rownames(pca_scores_df_species) # Add species as a column if not already
head(pca_scores_df_species)
write.csv(pca_scores_df_species, file = "PCA_Spore_Scores_Species.csv", row.names = FALSE)

```


```{r}
# Standardize species names in PCA dataset (e.g., Amanita_abrupta_Bas_1 -> A_abrupta)
pca_scores_df_species <- pca_scores_df_species %>%
  mutate(species = str_replace(species, "Amanita_", "A_"),     # Replace 'Amanita_' with 'A_'
         species = str_extract(species, "^A_[a-z]+"))          # Keep only 'A_speciesname'

# Check results
unique(pca_scores_df_species$species)

```
```{r}
# Aggregate PCA scores by species using summarise_at (alternative to across)
pca_agg <- pca_scores_df_species %>%
  group_by(species) %>%
  summarise_at(vars(starts_with("PC")), mean, na.rm = TRUE)

# Check the aggregated PCA scores
head(pca_agg)

```
```{r}
volume_data <- volume_data %>%
  mutate(species = str_replace(species, "Amanita_", "A_"),    # In case full names are used
         species = str_extract(species, "^A_[a-z]+"))         # Keep 'A_species' format

# Check species names after standardization
unique(volume_data$species)


```
# data merge 
```{r}
# Merge the PCA and volume datasets
merged_data <- inner_join(pca_agg, volume_data, by = "species")

# View the merged dataset
head(merged_data)

```

# visualize merged data

```{r}

# Correlation test
cor_test_result <- cor.test(merged_data$estimated_volume, merged_data$PC1)
cor_coef <- round(cor_test_result$estimate, 3)   # Correlation coefficient
p_value <- signif(cor_test_result$p.value, 3)    # p-value

# Linear regression model
lm_model <- lm(PC1 ~ estimated_volume, data = merged_data)
lm_summary <- summary(lm_model)
r_squared <- round(lm_summary$r.squared, 3)      # R-squared
slope <- round(coef(lm_model)[2], 3)             # Slope
intercept <- round(coef(lm_model)[1], 3)         # Intercept
```




```{r}


# Identify the point with the lowest spore volume (X-axis)
lowest_volume_point <- merged_data %>%
  filter(estimated_volume == min(estimated_volume))

# Identify the point with the lowest PC1 score (Y-axis)
lowest_PC1_point <- merged_data %>%
  filter(PC1 == min(PC1))

# Identify the top-right point (max volume and PC1)
top_right_point <- merged_data %>%
  filter(estimated_volume == max(estimated_volume) & PC1 == max(PC1))

# Enhanced plot with separate min labels and top-right label
ggplot(merged_data, aes(x = estimated_volume, y = PC1)) +
  geom_point(color = "darkorange", size = 4, alpha = 0.7, shape = 16) +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = FALSE, color = "steelblue", size = 1.5) +
  
  # Regression and correlation annotations
  annotate(
    "text", x = max(merged_data$estimated_volume) * 0.6,
    y = max(merged_data$PC1) * 0.9,
    label = paste0(
      "Correlation (r): ", round(cor.test(merged_data$estimated_volume, merged_data$PC1)$estimate, 3), "\n",
      "p-value: ", signif(cor.test(merged_data$estimated_volume, merged_data$PC1)$p.value, 3), "\n",
      "R²: ", round(summary(lm(PC1 ~ estimated_volume, data = merged_data))$r.squared, 3)
    ),
    size = 4, hjust = 0, color = "black"
  ) +

  # Label the point with the lowest spore volume (X-axis)
  geom_label(
    data = lowest_volume_point, aes(label = species),
    nudge_x = -0.05 * max(merged_data$estimated_volume),
    nudge_y = 0.05 * max(merged_data$PC1),
    color = "black", fill = "lightgreen", size = 3
  ) +

  # Label the point with the lowest PC1 score (Y-axis)
  geom_label(
    data = lowest_PC1_point, aes(label = species),
    nudge_x = 0.05 * max(merged_data$estimated_volume),
    nudge_y = -0.05 * max(merged_data$PC1),
    color = "black", fill = "lightpink", size = 3
  ) +

  # Label the top-right point (max volume and PC1)
  geom_label(
    data = top_right_point, aes(label = species),
    nudge_x = 0.05 * max(merged_data$estimated_volume),
    nudge_y = 0.05 * max(merged_data$PC1),
    color = "black", fill = "lightblue", size = 3
  ) +

  labs(
    title = "PC1 (Spore Shape) vs. Spore Volume",
    x = "Estimated Spore Volume (µm³)",
    y = "PC1 Score (Shape Variation)"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 18) +
  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(size = 20, face = "bold", hjust = 0.5),
    axis.title = element_text(size = 18, face = "bold"),
    axis.text = element_text(size = 16),
    aspect.ratio = 1
  )

```

```{r}

# Load the niche data
niche_data <- read.csv("spreadsheets/Spores_Amanita_ecological_niche.csv")

# Standardize species names in the niche dataset
niche_data <- niche_data %>%
  mutate(species = str_replace(species, "Amanita_", "A_"),
         species = str_extract(species, "^A_[a-z]+"))

# Add readable niche labels
niche_data <- niche_data %>%
  mutate(Ecology_label = case_when(
    Ecology == 1 ~ "Ectomycorrhizal (EM)",
    Ecology == 2 ~ "Saprotrophic (SAP)",
    TRUE ~ NA_character_
  ))

# Merge niche data with PCA + volume dataset
merged_pca_size_niche <- merged_data %>%
  left_join(niche_data %>% select(species, Ecology_label), by = "species") %>%
  filter(!is.na(Ecology_label))

# Define custom colors
niche_colors <- c("Ectomycorrhizal (EM)" = "green", "Saprotrophic (SAP)" = "orange")

# Create the combined plot
combined_plot <- ggplot(merged_pca_size_niche, aes(x = PC1, y = estimated_volume, color = Ecology_label)) +
  geom_point(size = 4, alpha = 0.7) +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = FALSE, size = 1.5, aes(color = Ecology_label)) +
  scale_color_manual(values = niche_colors) +
  labs(
    title = "PC1 (Spore Shape) vs. Spore Volume Colored by Ecological Niche",
    x = "PC1 Score (Shape Variation)",
    y = "Estimated Spore Volume (µm³)",
    color = "Ecological Niche"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 18) +
  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(size = 20, face = "bold", hjust = 0.5),
    axis.title = element_text(size = 18, face = "bold"),
    axis.text = element_text(size = 16),
    legend.position = "top",
    aspect.ratio = 1
  )

# Display the combined plot
print(combined_plot)


```

```{r}

merged_pca_size_niche %>%
  group_by(Ecology_label) %>%
  summarise(
    correlation = round(cor(PC1, estimated_volume, method = "pearson"), 3),
    p_value = signif(cor.test(PC1, estimated_volume)$p.value, 3)
  )

```



```{r}

# Calculate correlation and p-values per ecological niche manually
correlation_stats <- merged_pca_size_niche %>%
  group_split(Ecology_label) %>%
  lapply(function(df) {
    data.frame(
      Ecology_label = unique(df$Ecology_label),
      correlation = round(cor(df$PC1, df$estimated_volume, method = "pearson"), 3),
      p_value = signif(cor.test(df$PC1, df$estimated_volume)$p.value, 3)
    )
  }) %>%
  bind_rows() %>%
  mutate(
    x_pos = max(merged_pca_size_niche$PC1) * 0.6,
    y_pos = seq(from = max(merged_pca_size_niche$estimated_volume) * 0.95,
                by = -max(merged_pca_size_niche$estimated_volume) * 0.1,
                length.out = n())
  )

# Create the combined plot with p-value annotations
combined_plot_with_p <- ggplot(merged_pca_size_niche, aes(x = PC1, y = estimated_volume, color = Ecology_label)) +
  geom_point(size = 4, alpha = 0.7) +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = FALSE, size = 1.5, aes(color = Ecology_label)) +
  scale_color_manual(values = niche_colors) +
  labs(
    title = "PC1 (Spore Shape) vs. Spore Volume Colored by Ecological Niche",
    x = "PC1 Score (Shape Variation)",
    y = "Estimated Spore Volume (µm³)",
    color = "Ecological Niche"
  ) +
  # Correct annotation for correlation and p-values
  geom_text(
    data = correlation_stats,
    aes(
      x = x_pos,
      y = y_pos,
      label = paste0(Ecology_label, "\n", "r = ", correlation, ", p = ", p_value)
    ),
    size = 5, hjust = 0, inherit.aes = FALSE, color = "black"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 18) +
  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(size = 20, face = "bold", hjust = 0.5),
    axis.title = element_text(size = 18, face = "bold"),
    axis.text = element_text(size = 16),
    legend.position = "top",
    aspect.ratio = 1
  )

# Display the plot
print(combined_plot_with_p)


```

```{r}


# Extract top 5 for each extreme of both axes (with ecological niche)
top_largest_volume <- merged_pca_size_niche %>%
  arrange(desc(estimated_volume)) %>%
  slice_head(n = 5) %>%
  mutate(category = "Largest Spore Volume")

top_smallest_volume <- merged_pca_size_niche %>%
  arrange(estimated_volume) %>%
  slice_head(n = 5) %>%
  mutate(category = "Smallest Spore Volume")

top_elongate_spores <- merged_pca_size_niche %>%
  arrange(desc(PC1)) %>%
  slice_head(n = 5) %>%
  mutate(category = "Most Elongate Spores (High PC1)")

top_globose_spores <- merged_pca_size_niche %>%
  arrange(PC1) %>%
  slice_head(n = 5) %>%
  mutate(category = "Most Globose Spores (Low PC1)")

# Combine all and remove duplicates by species
top_extremes_combined <- bind_rows(
  top_largest_volume,
  top_smallest_volume,
  top_elongate_spores,
  top_globose_spores
) %>%
  distinct(species, .keep_all = TRUE)  # Remove duplicates

# View the final list of extremes
top_extremes_combined %>%
  select(species, estimated_volume, PC1, Ecology_label, category)

# Define niche colors
niche_colors <- c("Ectomycorrhizal (EM)" = "green", "Saprotrophic (SAP)" = "orange")

# Plot highlighting the extremes with ecological niche colors
extremes_plot <- ggplot(merged_pca_size_niche, aes(x = PC1, y = estimated_volume, color = Ecology_label)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.4, size = 3, shape = 16) +  # Background points
  geom_point(data = top_extremes_combined, aes(color = Ecology_label, shape = category), size = 6) +
  geom_label_repel(
    data = top_extremes_combined,
    aes(label = species),
    size = 5, box.padding = 0.5, point.padding = 0.5, max.overlaps = Inf,
    segment.color = "grey50", force = 2
  ) +
  scale_color_manual(values = niche_colors) +
  scale_shape_manual(values = c(15, 16, 17, 18)) +  # Different shapes per category
  labs(
    title = "Top 5 Extremes of Spore Shape and Volume (with Ecological Niche)",
    x = "PC1 Score (Shape Variation: Globose to Elongate)",
    y = "Estimated Spore Volume (µm³)",
    color = "Ecological Niche",
    shape = "Category"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 18) +
  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(size = 20, face = "bold", hjust = 0.5),
    axis.title = element_text(size = 18, face = "bold"),
    axis.text = element_text(size = 16),
    legend.title = element_text(size = 16),
    legend.text = element_text(size = 14),
    legend.position = "top",
    aspect.ratio = 1
  )

# Display the plot
print(extremes_plot)


```

# Weather and PC1 and Shape analysis -----------------------------------


```{r}


# Select only numeric variables for correlation analysis
numeric_vars <- merged_pca_size_niche_weather_geography[, c("avg_temp", "min_temp", "max_temp", "Precipitation", "PC1", "estimated_volume")]

# Compute correlation matrix with significance (p-values)
cor_results <- rcorr(as.matrix(numeric_vars), type = "pearson")  # Use "spearman" if needed

cor_matrix <- cor_results$r  # Correlation values
p_matrix <- cor_results$P    # P-values

# Convert correlation matrix to long format
cor_melted <- melt(cor_matrix)
p_melted <- melt(p_matrix)

# Merge correlation and p-values
cor_melted$p_value <- p_melted$value

# Function to format p-values for display
cor_melted$significance <- ifelse(cor_melted$p_value < 0.01, "**", 
                           ifelse(cor_melted$p_value < 0.05, "*", ""))

```

```{r}

write.csv(p_matrix, file = "p_matrix.csv", row.names = FALSE)

```

```{r}
# Create the heatmap with a white background and clear labels
Correlation_heatmap <- ggplot(cor_melted, aes(x=Var1, y=Var2, fill=value)) + 
  geom_tile(color="white") +
  
  # Add correlation values with significance markers
  geom_text(aes(label=sprintf("%.2f%s", value, significance)), 
            size=6, fontface="bold", color="black") +  
  
  # Improve color scale with better contrast
  scale_fill_gradient2(low="blue", high="red", mid="white", midpoint=0, 
                       limit=c(-1,1), name="Correlation") +  
  
  # Apply a white background theme
  theme_classic() +  

  # Titles and labels
  labs(
    title="Correlation Heatmap with P-values",
    subtitle="Significance levels: **p < 0.01, *p < 0.05",
  ) +

  # Improve axis readability
  theme(
    axis.text.x = element_text(angle=45, hjust=1, size=14, face="bold"),  
    axis.text.y = element_text(size=14, face="bold"),  
    plot.title = element_text(size=16, face="bold"),  
    plot.subtitle = element_text(size=12, face="italic"),  # Subtitle explaining asterisks
    plot.caption = element_text(size=12, face="italic"),  # Caption for p-value significance
    legend.text = element_text(size=12),  
    legend.title = element_text(size=14, face="bold"),
    
    # Ensure panel background is completely white
    panel.background = element_rect(fill="white", color=NA),
    plot.background = element_rect(fill="white", color=NA)
  )


```

```{r}

# Save the plot
ggsave("Correlation_heatmap.png",
       plot = Correlation_heatmap, width = 12, height = 12, dpi = 300)


```

# Precipitation vs pc1

```{r}


# Compute Pearson correlation and get the p-value
cor_test <- rcorr(as.matrix(merged_pca_size_niche_weather_geography[, c("Precipitation", "PC1")]), type = "pearson")
p_value_pc1_precip <- cor_test$P[1,2]  # Extract p-value

# Convert p-value to formatted string for display
p_label <- paste("p =", format.pval(p_value_pc1_precip, digits = 3, scientific = TRUE))

```

```{r}


# Scatter plot: Precipitation vs PC1
scatter_plot <- ggplot(merged_pca_size_niche_weather_geography, 
                       aes(x = Precipitation, y = PC1, label = species, size = estimated_volume)) +
  
  # Make dot sizes more dramatic
  geom_point(color = "blue", alpha = 0.7) +
  scale_size(range = c(3, 10)) +  # Increase size difference between smallest & largest points
  
  # Add regression line with confidence interval
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", color = "red", se = TRUE, linetype = "dashed", fill = "grey70") +
  
  # Add labels for species names with repelling to avoid overlap
  geom_text_repel(size = 5, fontface = "bold", color = "black") +
  
  # Add p-value annotation on the plot
  annotate("text", x = max(merged_pca_size_niche_weather_geography$Precipitation) - 1, 
           y = max(merged_pca_size_niche_weather_geography$PC1), 
           label = p_label, size = 6, fontface = "bold", color = "red") +

  # Titles and labels
  labs(
    title = "Precipitation vs PC1",
    subtitle = "Point size represents estimated spore volume",
    x = "Precipitation (mm)",
    y = "PC1 Score"
  ) +
  
  # Theme adjustments for readability & remove legend
  theme_classic(base_size = 14) +
  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(size = 18, face = "bold"),
    plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 14, face = "italic"),
    axis.text = element_text(size = 12, face = "bold"),
    axis.title = element_text(size = 14, face = "bold"),
    legend.position = "none",  # Remove legend
    panel.background = element_rect(fill = "white", color = "black"),
    plot.background = element_rect(fill = "white", color = NA)
  )

# Save the plot
ggsave("Precipitation_vs_PC1_updated.png", plot = scatter_plot, width = 10, height = 8, dpi = 300)

# Print plot
print(scatter_plot)


```






# Geography and pc1 and shape analysis -----------------------------------


```{r}

# Check normality of PC1
shapiro_test_pc1 <- shapiro.test(merged_pca_size_niche_weather_geography$PC1)
print(shapiro_test_pc1)
```

```{r}

# Check normality of estimated_volume
shapiro_test_volume <- shapiro.test(merged_pca_size_niche_weather_geography$estimated_volume)
print(shapiro_test_volume)

```

# the following only applies if the above fails the normality test aka p-value < 0.05
```{r}

# Perform Kruskal-Wallis test for PC1
kw_pc1 <- kruskal.test(PC1 ~ Geography_Estimated, data = merged_pca_size_niche_weather_geography)
print("Kruskal-Wallis test for PC1:")
print(kw_pc1)

# Perform Kruskal-Wallis test for estimated volume
kw_volume <- kruskal.test(estimated_volume ~ Geography_Estimated, data = merged_pca_size_niche_weather_geography)
print("Kruskal-Wallis test for Estimated Volume:")
print(kw_volume)

```


```{r}
# Post-hoc Dunn's test (only if Kruskal-Wallis is significant)
if (kw_pc1$p.value < 0.05) {
  dunn_pc1 <- dunn.test(data$PC1, data$Geography_Estimated, method = "bonferroni")
  print("Post-hoc Dunn’s Test for PC1:")
  print(dunn_pc1)
}

if (kw_volume$p.value < 0.05) {
  dunn_volume <- dunn.test(data$estimated_volume, data$Geography_Estimated, method = "bonferroni")
  print("Post-hoc Dunn’s Test for Estimated Volume:")
  print(dunn_volume)
}


```

# the following only applies if the above fails the normality test aka p-value < 0.05
